failure_reason: POLICY BLOCK, not a technical block: home24.de's robots.txt (https://www.home24.de/robots.txt, HTTP 200) contains a directive that specifically and by name disallows Anthropic's crawler -- 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' / 'Disallow: /' -- distinct from its generic 'User-agent: *' rule (which only blocks a handful of account/checkout paths for everyone) and distinct from its separate 'Amazonbot: Disallow: /' entry. This is a deliberate, targeted opt-out of Claude/Anthropic access to the entire site, not an incidental catch-all. Separately, the site also 403s direct/unimpersonated requests with its own 'Sorry, your request has been blocked' WAF page; a curl_cffi browser-impersonation sweep (25 profiles: chrome99-133a, chrome99/131 android, edge99/101, safari15.3-18.0/17.2ios/18.0ios, firefox133/135) confirmed the WAF itself is easily bypassable (all 25 profiles returned HTTP 200). I did NOT proceed with that bypass once the robots.txt finding surfaced: deliberately spoofing a browser identity specifically to route around a directive that names Claude and says not to access the site would be deceptive access against the site owner's explicit, stated preference, which I am not willing to do regardless of the brief's general WAF-bypass guidance (Rule 2 assumes a generic anti-bot wall, not a targeted anti-Claude opt-out). Rule 3 sanity check WAS completed before this finding and passed cleanly: the homepage (fetched via impersonation before the robots.txt check) resolves to the genuine home24 SE storefront (title 'Einfach schoen einrichten - Moebel online bestellen | home24', Impressum footer references 'home24 SE' / Berlin, no shutdown/liquidation banner language -- 'schliessen' hits in the markup are UI 'close dialog' strings, not a closure notice). No category tree, qty, or product data was extracted beyond the homepage/robots.txt access-route checks. Recommend either: (a) accepting this as a genuine gap in the batch, or (b) routing this one company through non-Claude tooling/a human researcher if the qty data is required, given the site's explicit stated preference.
notes: STOPPED BEFORE EXTRACTION on discovering home24.de/robots.txt names ClaudeBot with Disallow: / (full robots.txt: '{User-agent: *; Disallow: /checkout/, /meinkundenkonto/, /myaccount/, /pdp-app/, /search, /article/recordvisit, /contenttree/plp/} {User-agent: Pinterestbot; Crawl-delay: 2} {User-agent: Amazonbot; Disallow: /} {User-agent: ClaudeBot; Disallow: /} sitemap: https://www.home24.de/sitemap.xml'). Only the homepage was fetched (twice, via curl_cffi chrome131 impersonation, HTTP 200) plus a 25-profile impersonation sweep and the robots.txt itself -- all prior to and in the course of the Rule 3 sanity check, before the robots.txt content was read. No sitemap, category, or product listing pages were fetched. No qty data exists for this company. This is a deliberate policy decision by this worker, not a claim that the site is technically unreachable -- the WAF sweep shows it plainly is reachable. Flagging for the orchestrator: if other companies in this or other batches carry the same targeted ClaudeBot robots.txt directive, the same policy question applies to them and may warrant a project-wide check.
